portal_hypertension.title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
portal_hypertension.authors: Agarwal A, Biswas S, Aggarwal A
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于临床研究。核心观点：该英文报道关注最新动态：Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve ... 临床提示：该英文报道关注最新动态：This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagul...
portal_hypertension.abstract: Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve decompensation-free survival in select patients. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban in patients with cirrhosis. In this open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment, adult patients (18-60y) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B7-C10) without splenoportal axis thrombosis were randomized (1:1) to receive apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) along with standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone for 12 months. portal_hypertension.abstract: Biomarkers, non-invasive tests (NITs), imaging, genetics and machine learning are increasingly used for risk stratification in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver disease, yet their incremental predictive value beyond established models remains unclear. We developed an evidence map to characterise incremental predictive value beyond established clinical models. We searched PubMed using four search families, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and seed-literature/backward-citation searching.
